description: I'm saheer, a second year BTECH AI & ML student at ACE College of engineering, Trivandrum. I work with python and data automation, and building small, practical projects with real data. I'm taking part visually and want to finish a clear, working project for this challenge. We are six friends taking part in the NASA Space Apps Challenge virtually. We are responsible, curious and motivated, and we enjoy learning and working together. We want to build a clear, working project using NASA data and submit it on time.
summary:
SUMMARY:
We built a small Python tool that takes any Earth-science time series, removes the seasonal cycle, fits a linear trend with a 95% confidence interval, and tests significance using regression and the Mann-Kendall test. We applied it to NASA MERRA-2 monthly 2-metre air temperature (2000–2024, from NASA Giovanni) for two regions: Kerala and the Rajasthan desert. Kerala shows a significant warming trend of about +0.30 K per decade (p < 0.001, confirmed on yearly averages). The Rajasthan desert shows a significant cooling trend of about −0.32 K per decade (yearly p = 0.013). So the same variable trends in opposite directions in two regions, which is exactly the kind of regional difference the challenge describes. Reanalysis data is model-assisted, so we report these as trends in the dataset, not as direct station measurements.
